blocks.x: Do you know what your travel love language is? In the early 1990s, the concept of five love languages—words of affirmation, quality time, receiving gifts, acts of service, and physical touch—was popularized, supposedly to help partners, families, and parents understand each other’s needs and respond accordingly.

But travel introduces a whole other set of variables. Travel can, at times, bring out the worst in people. Long airport queues, flight delays, and lost luggage are reason enough for anyone to lose their temper. Add in travel stress, jet lag, and potentially a headache or two from late-night beers, and you’ve got a recipe for disaster. So, our editors set out to establish the love languages of travel: the character types and personalities that describe most travelers, so you can better prepare for your next trip (and decide who you should—or shouldn't—hop on a plane with).

Communication is key, and part of that is figuring out what type of person suits you for travel. If you are, for example, a hyper-organized, time-vigilant traveler, then perhaps you should avoid traveling with someone who loves a spontaneous excursion. Or, if you’re an early bird, consider traveling with a culture vulture—someone to spend those precious morning hours with, to squeeze in a visit to a gallery or café that gets too busy later in the day. Below, explore which love language you abide by.
The Planner

blocks.x: The Planner leaves no detail overlooked.
Getty Images

More often than not, the Planner is the one who organized the entire trip. Think of them as the operations manager of the holiday: This is the person who curates the itineraries, makes the schedules, and books the tickets. They’re Type A through and through. They make things happen, but they can clash with certain travelers (and, more often than not, their best friend/partner/sibling has the exact opposite travel love language).

“I'm a pretty intense Type-A planner in all parts of my life, but travel is where I come into my own,” says Chloe Laws, acting audience growth manager at Conde Nast Traveller UK. “I've learned, though, from marriage to a Type-B traveler and being surrounded by many friends who want to go with the flow, not to enforce it on other people. Gently suggest, yes, perhaps even keep a personal itinerary that I pretend is spontaneous, but try and let everyone choose their own plans—it's their holiday, too. And if they end up going to a few bad restaurants because they've not done enough research, so be it."

Don’t travel with: The Culture Vulture. This traveler follows their nose, constantly seeking under-the-radar spots to uncover. Of course, there are times when your tastes align, but if you don’t discuss plans in advance, friction will arise.

Where to travel: A European city break. Museums, galleries, and walking tours galore, plus endless options of restaurants for perfectly timed dinner reservations. Think Porto, Marseille, or Turin—cities that are a little offbeat, but offer everything you’re looking for in a holiday destination.

Remember to pack: Chances are, you’ve already made a packing list, so you don’t need us to tell you what to pack. Just remember, a touch of spontaneity goes a long way when you’re traveling. If you adjust timings or skip a reservation to follow your gut once in a while, you might stumble upon some truly amazing experiences.

blocks.c: Image may contain Photography Book Comics Publication Person Art Face and Head

blocks.x: The Photographer is the utmost documentarian.
Getty Images
The Photographer

Ah, the aesthete. Everyone’s favorite traveler. This is the person with the eye for beauty; they’ll spy a table with a view, a cute cobbled street for a drink, a perfect spot to watch the sunset from a mile off. They’re often very laidback, happy to go with the flow and see where the day takes them. The Photographer also doubles up as the wardrobe coordinator: the person on the trip who often has the best outfits that everyone ends up borrowing.
Don’t travel with: You're a cool customer, so a trip with anyone and everyone is fine with you.

Where to travel: Anywhere with high vantage points. You’ll be happy in any destination that scratches that itch you have to find beauty. Plan a hiking tour around the Cliffs of Moher in Ireland, hop on a ski lift in the Alps for mountain views, or go stargazing in New Zealand (and make sure to have that wide-angle lens properly exposed). If you're more a street documentarian, head to London for the many craftspeople keeping its traditions alive or Montreal for a vibrant shopping scene.
Remember to pack: Chargers, chargers, and more chargers. The last thing you want is to be caught with a drained battery and no way to snap the perfect shot.
https://media.cntraveler.com/photos/6ab529993d02bf24601bcf2a/master/w_1600%2Cc_limit/The-Treasurer.jpg
blocks.c: Image may contain People Person Clothing Hat Adult Cap Wedding and Photography

blocks.x: The Treasurer ensures everyone is paying their part, down to the cent.
Getty Images
The Treasurer

Roles don’t get much more important than this. This is the CFO of all holidays, the person who keeps track of money and constantly updates Splitwise. They work well with the Planner, plotting side by side to make sure everything is nicely squared away and plans are running smoothly. Their talents extend beyond just money; they like a challenge and enjoy calculating the best way to keep everyone happy.
Don’t travel with: The Night Owl. They relish a spontaneous night out that ends up emptying the rest of the trip’s allocated spend.

Where to travel: The Treasurer loves nothing more than a wallet-friendly holiday, and our favorite affordable cities in the US are a good start—consider Charleston, San Diego, or Phoenix. Looking for luxe on a budget? New Mexico's arty Hotel Willa, sleek Fairmont Mumbai, and scenic Inkaterra Cabo Blanco in Peru all have rates that start below $300.

Remember to pack: A trusty travel wallet with additional pockets for currency, keys, your phone, SIM cards, and the like, so you’re ready and waiting for each opportunity to demonstrate your organizational abilities.
https://media.cntraveler.com/photos/6ab529993d02bf24601bcf2b/master/w_1600%2Cc_limit/The-Navigator.jpg
blocks.c: Image may contain Person Worker Adult People Face and Head

Getty Images
The Navigator

A valued member of any group trip. This person is the map reader, the one with an innate sense of direction, a built-in compass, someone who can direct the gang back to the Airbnb without so much as checking Google Maps.
Don’t travel with: The Culture Vulture. This traveler loves nothing more than squeezing in an extra trip to another tiny gallery in some remote part of town.

Where to travel: A walkable city to test your skills and flânerie. The labyrinthine Marrakech will do the trick, where you can spend hours weaving your way through the backstreets and stumbling upon hidden gems and lesser-known spots.
Remember to pack: Brightly-colored clothing, and possibly a hat, so your fellow travelers can spot you easily and follow along.
